title: An Introduction to lambertReg
text: lambertReg fits sparse Gaussian regression Lambert penalty. main functions lambert() regularization path cv.lambert() choosing penalty strength cross-validation. provide coefficient extraction, prediction, plotting methods. guide follows one example fitting prediction new data. training sample n observations p predictors, package targets penalized least-squares objective    Q_\lambda(b)=\frac{1}{2n}\lVert y_c-Zb\rVert_2^2+   \sum_{j=1}^p p_\lambda(|b_j|).  b\\mathbb R^p contains standardized coefficients, y_c centered response, Z centered scaled training matrix. intercept unpenalized. parameter \lambda>0 controls strength Lambert penalty p_\lambda, whose shape fixed c=1. penalty becomes constant coefficient magnitudes e\lambda . Cyclic coordinate updates seek stationary solution; global minimum guaranteed nonconvex objective.

title: An Introduction to lambertReg
text: example 100 observations, eight predictors, three nonzero coefficients. use 80 observations training reserve 20 prediction. test observations enter preprocessing tuning.
code: library(lambertReg) set.seed(42) x <- matrix(rnorm(100 * 8), nrow = 100, ncol = 8) colnames(x) <- paste0("x", seq_len(ncol(x))) y <- 2 * x[, 1] - x[, 2] + 0.5 * x[, 3] + rnorm(100) train <- seq_len(80) x_train <- x[train, , drop = FALSE] y_train <- y[train] x_test <- x[-train, , drop = FALSE] y_test <- y[-train]

title: An Introduction to lambertReg

title: An Introduction to lambertReg
text: Within training sample, predictor j centered mean \bar x_j divided centered root-mean-square value s_j=\{n^{-1}\sum_{=1}^n(x_{ij}-\bar x_j)^2\}^{1/2}. Thus Z_{ij}=(x_{ij}-\bar x_j)/s_j squared column norm n. response centered training mean variance-scaled. CV estimates quantities using training observations fold. entry score \lambda_{\max}=\max_j|Z_j^\top y_c|/n, Z_j column j standardized design, defines upper end relative path. candidate fraction \tau_k\(0,1] fold f, penalty \lambda_{k,f}=\tau_k\lambda_{\max,f}. CV therefore compares common fractions, absolute penalties can differ folds. score averages fold MSEs arithmetically, including folds unequal sizes. Numerical ties favor larger fraction. custom fractional grid must positive, strictly decreasing, larger one. Absolute penalties can instead supplied lambert(): scalar penalty coordinate threshold also available directly. magnitude t\geq0, lambert_penalty(t, lambda) evaluates p_\lambda(t); lambert_threshold(z, lambda) applies scalar update partial-residual score z standardized coordinate unit curvature.
code: fractions <- 10^seq(0, -3, length.out = 80L) fit_custom <- cv.lambert(x_train, y_train, foldid = foldid,                         lambda_fraction = fractions) path_absolute <- lambert(x_train, y_train, lambda = path$lambda) z <- c(-3, -1, 0, 1, 3) knitr::kable(data.frame(   Score = z,   Penalty_at_magnitude = lambert_penalty(abs(z), lambda = 1),   Updated_coefficient = lambert_threshold(z, lambda = 1) ), digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)

title: The Fixed Lambert Penalty and Scalar Update — lambert_penalty
text: Write \(W_0\) principal real Lambert function, characterized \(W_0(u)\exp(W_0(u))=u\) \(u\geq0\). magnitude \(t\), let \(w=W_0(t/\lambda)\). penalty $$p_\lambda(t)=\frac{\lambda^2}{4}  [e^{2w}(1+2w-2w^2)-1],\quad 0\leq t\leq e\lambda.$$ \(t>e\lambda\), constant \(\lambda^2(e^2-1)/4\). expression evaluated cancellation-resistant arithmetic near zero. scalar update minimizes \((z-b)^2/2+p_\lambda(|b|)\) \(b\R\). zero \(|z|\leq\lambda\), equals \(z\log(|z|/\lambda)\) \(\lambda<|z|<e\lambda\), equals \(z\) \(|z|\geq e\lambda\). normalization requires unit coordinate curvature, obtained training-RMS scaling lambert.

title: Inspect and Predict from Lambert Fits — predict.lambert
code: set.seed(42) x <- matrix(rnorm(40 * 4), 40, 4) colnames(x) <- paste0("x", 1:4) y <- x[, 1] - x[, 2] + rnorm(40) cv <- cv.lambert(x, y, foldid = rep(1:5, each = 8),                  lambda_fraction = c(1, .3, .1)) plot(cv)  plot(cv, style = "paper")  plot(cv, type = "coefficients", labels = TRUE)  plot(cv$lambert.fit, style = "paper")
